conversions.description: In-state street-legal conversion filings in the states that actually allow your vehicle class — Arizona, Utah, South Dakota, West Virginia, Michigan assembled-vehicle retitling — with the correct checklist for each.
conversions.h1: Street-legal where your state actually allows it.
conversions.intro: About twenty states have a real, statewide path to put a UTV, ATV, or off-highway motorcycle on the road — in your state, under your state's equipment list, with your state's plate. That is the lawful version of what the plate-export ads gesture at, and it's the version that survives a traffic stop, an insurance claim, and a resale. TorqueTitles files in-state conversions state by state, with the correct checklist for each — never a copied one.

paras: The lawful routes are: a factory street-legal/dual-sport motorcycle; a state class that expressly includes off-highway motorcycles (Utah's does); or assembled-vehicle retitling (Michigan). If your state has none of the three, there is no filing we can sell you — and anyone who sells you one anyway is selling you a citation and impound risk.

list: Arizona: MVD street-legal registration plus the $25/yr OHV decal; equipment includes brake/brake light, headlights visible 500 ft, taillight, horn audible 200 ft, muffler, mirror, and eye protection or a windshield.

Utah: Street-legal ATV registration under Utah Code §41-6a-1509 — full lighting/turn-signal/mirror/speedometer/seatbelt list, motorcycle-size plate, no interstates, speed capped at the posted limit or 50 mph.
South Dakota: ATV licensed as a motorcycle under SDCL §32-20-13 (affidavit + title/MSO at the county treasurer), no interstate highways.

West Virginia: “Street-legal special purpose vehicle” under W. Va. Code §17A-13-1 — a class that expressly includes ATVs, UTVs, mini-trucks, and pneumatic-tired military vehicles; motorcycle-size plate, no controlled-access highways, max 20 miles on centreline-marked highways, local opt-outs apply.

Michigan (the premium route): Michigan has no UTV class — the vehicle is retitled as an Assembled Vehicle (MCL §257.217i): safety-glass windshield with wipers and washers, the full lighting/brake/belt/mirror list, two inspections, and the state issues a new VIN. It takes about 3–4 months, and the result is the most portable UTV outcome in the country: a motor-vehicle title other states recognise as a motor vehicle. Sold as our White Glove filing ($1,499) or by written quote, with the timeline stated before you pay.

Conditional states, sold as conditional: Minnesota and Indiana are county/local-permit states (Indiana's BMV will not plate an ORV at all; out-of-state ORV registration is honoured there for at most 20 days a year). Kansas micro-utility trucks are barred from interstate/federal/state highways. We sell these as local-use filings with the limits printed on the quote — never as statewide freedom.

Prohibition states, sold as nothing: Texas law bars TxDMV from registering an off-highway vehicle for highway use “with or without alterations” (Transp. Code §502.140; its ≤$10 plate is for limited uses only). California cannot convert ATVs, and CARB status is dispositive. Florida has no UTV/ROV road class (see the Florida desk). In these states we will not sell you a conversion filing, and an out-of-state plate does not change the answer.
paras: Examples — your screen uses your state's actual list.

Eligibility screen for your state and vehicle class; equipment checklist with photo verification; kit guidance (we'll tell you which listed components your state actually requires — hardware is yours to buy/install, or through a partner installer where available); the complete filing packet; inspection scheduling prep; and stage tracking on the one timeline.

domicile.intro: Most filing businesses disappear after the plate ships. The money and the risk both live in year two: a Montana LLC that misses its 15 April annual report imperils the registration it holds; a South Dakota registration renews annually; a domicile that isn't maintained stops being a domicile. This desk is the subscription that keeps every filing we've touched current — and the honest route into (and out of) Montana.

Reminders at 60/30/7 days for anything that can lapse. Lapses are how registrations die; we treat the calendar as part of the product.

sections.h: Genuine full-time travellers: South Dakota domicile
paras: If you truly live on the road — no fixed garaging state — South Dakota deliberately accommodates you: a Residency Affidavit supported by a lodging receipt and a mail-forwarding (PMB) address, a driver's licence after a one-night stay, and vehicle registration handled by mail or by an agent under power of attorney. We arrange this through established domicile/mail-forwarding partners (published partner pricing in the market runs $414–$599 for the first year, then $204–$360/year + $25 per vehicle) instead of pretending we're a South Dakota mail company.

Two honest disclosures: (1) since 2025, South Dakota requires 30 consecutive days in a fixed dwelling to vote in state/local elections — a licence and registration are not a state ballot; (2) “full-time traveller” is a fact test, not a form — if you actually garage the vehicle at a home in another state, that state's rules apply, and our screen will say so.

Montana LLC registration is lawful in Montana and still right for real profiles: vehicles genuinely garaged or stored in Montana, businesses with a real Montana nexus, collectors whose vehicles live in Montana, and true full-time travellers. It is filed through a Montana registered agent in the agent's county; state costs include the $35 LLC filing, ~$12 title, and registration from $217/year (newer light vehicles) down to $28, permanent plates at 11+ years ($87.50 one-time), permanent motorcycle/quadricycle registration ($53.25 street / $114.50 street + off-highway), and a +$825/year luxury surcharge on vehicles with MSRP over $150,000 under 11 years old.

It is not a tax product. If your vehicle will live in a state with a use tax and a resident-registration deadline, that state will very likely require its own registration and tax no matter whose name is on a Montana title — and several states now enforce exactly that, with personal liability for LLC members (California's SB 1406, effective 2026), insurance-data matching (Utah's SB 52 sweep flagged ~80,000 vehicles), doubled penalties (Georgia HB 551, from 1 January 2026), and criminal charges in California and Tennessee cases. That is why Montana intakes start with the six questions and a signed disclosure. If the screen says your profile is exposed, we decline or refer you to a tax professional — before payment, not after.
sections.priceLine: Core Montana prices (our service fee; government fees at cost, itemised): Powersports $749 · Cars/RVs $949 · White Glove $1,499 · Ownership Cover $99/yr. Financed vehicles usually route to South Dakota instead (4% excise tax + $100 non-resident title fee + $10 title, per the county's published schedule; the lienholder stays on the title) — the screen tells you which route your facts fit, and why.

florida.description: Florida-native vehicle filings done the Florida way: golf-cart-to-LSV conversion filings, estate vehicle transfers under Fla. Stat. §319.28, and rebuilt-title packets — with free triage and a written flat quote before any work begins.
florida.h1: Florida paperwork, done the Florida way.
florida.intro: Florida is where we live, and Florida does not work like the internet says it does. A Montana plate does not make a UTV legal on Florida roads. A golf cart is not a low-speed vehicle until Florida says it is. TorqueTitles files the Florida routes that actually exist — and we'll tell you plainly when the route you're asking about doesn't.

list: ATVs may be used on Florida public roads only in narrow circumstances (daytime, unpaved, posted under 35 mph, §316.2123). UTVs/ROVs have no equivalent road right, and dirt bikes that weren't manufactured street-legal have no Florida conversion path. We will not sell you a filing that pretends otherwise.
Florida residents must title/register within 10 days of bringing a vehicle into the state or establishing residency.

paras: A Florida golf cart tops out at 20 mph and cannot be titled or registered. To use one on Florida roads (posted 35 mph or less) it must become a low-speed vehicle: 20–25 mph, built to the federal LSV standard (49 CFR 571.500) — headlamps, stop/turn/tail lamps, reflectors, mirrors, a real FMVSS-205 windshield, seat belts, parking brake, and a VIN — then pass FLHSMV inspection, receive a Florida-assigned VIN, and be titled, registered, and insured (minimum $10,000 PIP + $10,000 PDL). Some vehicles manufactured as off-road vehicles are not eligible for LSV conversion at all; the screen checks this before you pay.

What we do: pre-inspection audit of your cart against the equipment list, the complete forms packet (HSMV 84490 / 86064 / 82040, TL-63 procedure), inspection scheduling prep, and the title/registration filing. What we don't do: sell you a “conversion kit” that fails inspection, or promise that a utility ATV can become an LSV when Florida says it can't.
sections.priceLine: Price: free triage → written flat quote before any work begins. Government fees (FLHSMV/county) at cost, itemised.

paras: When a vehicle owner dies, Florida lets a surviving spouse or the heirs transfer the vehicle without probate when the estate is not indebted and the spouse/all heirs agree (or, for a will, with the certified will and solvency affidavit). The paperwork is specific — HSMV 82040 (and 82152 for a spouse), death certificate, agreement of the heirs — and a wrong form restarts the clock at the tax collector. A spouse can also assign directly to a buyer without titling the vehicle in their own name first.

What we do: heirship document checklist, affidavit and form preparation, tax-collector filing, and multi-heir coordination when the family is spread across states. Title fee is ~$75.25 (government fee, at cost). If your estate doesn't meet the §319.28 conditions, we tell you and point you to the probate route instead of filing something that will be rejected.
sections.priceLine: Price: free triage → written flat quote before any work begins.

paras: A Florida salvage vehicle becomes road-legal one way: documented repairs, then a DHSMV/PRVIP physical examination ($40, $20 re-exam), then a title branded “Rebuilt” — permanently. Anyone who offers to make that brand disappear is offering fraud; we will not do it and neither should you. Selling a rebuilt vehicle before the examination and branding is a second-degree misdemeanour in Florida (§319.14(6)).

What we do: builder-statement packet (HSMV 84490), major-component parts-receipt audit (the #1 reason exams fail), exam scheduling, and the branded-title filing. You end with a vehicle you can insure, register, and sell honestly.

terms.intro: Last updated November 3, 2026. TorqueTitles is a service of LIFEOFMORR LLC, a Florida limited liability company. By submitting an intake you agree to these terms for the filing-preparation services described on this site.

paras: TorqueTitles is a private filing-preparation service. We are not a DMV, tax collector, Secretary of State, court, or any government agency, and we do not issue titles, plates, or registrations — government offices do. We prepare and submit paperwork as your agent. We do not provide tax or legal advice; questions about your tax duties or legal position belong to your own CPA or attorney.

Government offices decide outcomes and work on their own clocks. We publish expected government timelines honestly, but a government delay is not a service failure we can refund our way out of — see the guarantee below for exactly what is refundable.

No checkout is reachable before the eligibility screen. Green files receive their route and exact price in writing before payment. Amber files proceed only after the required signed disclosure or written acknowledgment and human review. Red files are declined and never receive a payment link. If any answer in your intake proves inaccurate, we may stop the filing; the guarantee below still applies as published.

Service fees are the published prices on the Pricing page (powersports $749; cars/RVs $949; White Glove $1,499; Ownership Cover $99/year) or a written flat quote given before work begins. Government and third-party costs (county/agency fees, surety premiums, partner charges) are itemised at cost and are separate from our service fee. Payment links are issued per file after the screen; paying a link someone forwarded to you does not create a filing — every paid file starts with its own intake.

Refund until filed. If you cancel before we submit your filing to the county or agency, we refund our service fee in full. If we cannot complete your filing, we refund our service fee in full. Government fees are refunded to the extent the government refunds them. No time windows, no deduction ladder, no store credit.

list: Your intake answers — garaging, use, connection, liens, title brands, insurance — must be complete and accurate; filings are prepared from them.

You remain responsible for your home state's registration, tax, insurance, and road-use duties. A registration we file in one state does not erase another state's duties, and no filing makes a vehicle legal to operate where its class is prohibited.
Keep your contact details and (for subscribers) your garaging state current in your file; law-change alerts and renewal reminders go to the details on record.

title-recovery.description: Lawful lanes for a real vehicle with a broken paper trail: bonded titles, court-ordered titles, lien-sale paperwork for shops and storage operators, and lost-title duplicates — free eligibility check first.
title-recovery.h1: No title? That's a paperwork problem. We solve paperwork problems.
title-recovery.intro: Every state has lawful lanes for a real vehicle with a broken paper trail. They are slower and more specific than the internet's “magic state” stories — the most famous of those (Vermont bill-of-sale titling) has been closed since July 2023 — and they work when they're done by the book. Start with a free eligibility check: tell us the vehicle, the state, and what paper you actually have. We route you to the lane that exists, or we tell you there isn't one.

note.h: What we will not do (title edition)
paras: No brand washing. No VIN workarounds. No “duplicate” for a vehicle you don't own. No back-dated bills of sale. If a previous owner, lienholder, or court has to be part of the answer, we tell you at triage — before money moves.

Most states; not a Florida lane for cars. The state sets a bond — commonly 1.5× the vehicle's value (some states 2×) — issued by a licensed surety. The premium is roughly 1–2% of the bond (published schedule benchmark: $100 flat up to a $6,699 bond, then $15 per $1,000). File within 30 days of buying the bond; bonded title in about 4–6 weeks; the brand clears after about 3 years. We handle valuation, bond placement with the licensed surety (we are not the surety; the premium is a pass-through at the surety's price), the packet, and the county filing — plus a reminder when your brand-clearing date arrives.

For states without a bonded lane and for contested paper. Court filing fees run $50–$450; a straightforward uncontested case typically totals $200–$800 in government/third-party costs and takes 2–6 months. We prepare the petition packet, order the title/lien search, manage notice/publication, and calendar the hearing. If your case is contested, we refer you to an attorney — we prepare paperwork; we don't practise law.

sections.h: Lien-sale paperwork (for shops, tow, and storage operators)
paras: Statutory lien sales are unforgiving: in the benchmark regime (California Civil Code §§3068–3074), authorisation must be sought within 30 days of the lien arising or the lien dies, and timelines run ~35–45 days (vehicles under $4,000) to ~90–150 days (above). We run the authorisation packet, owner/lienholder notices, publication, sale paperwork, and the buyer's title packet — per vehicle, on your state's checklist, built before we take your first unit.

A duplicate can only come from the state that issued the title, to the owner of record (or their POA/court representative). We locate the record state (including pre-title-era vehicles), verify identity and liens, and bundle the duplicate + transfer. If the title isn't yours to duplicate, we stop — that request is the fraud pattern, not a service.

Eligibility check: free. After triage you get a written packet price and the government/surety costs at their published schedules before you decide. If we take your case and cannot complete it, our fee is refunded under the Refund-Until-Filed guarantee (and after filing, if completion becomes impossible, our fee is still refunded — government and surety amounts only to the extent they are refunded to us).
